title: Document
description: A parsed source document: an optional scope header plus its declarations.

scope.description: The scope header, if the document opens with one.

Annotation.description: Provenance attached to a lore-bearing declaration.

condition.description:
Optional hypothesis condition under which the claim is asserted
(`assumes <hyp>`).

span.description: Where the annotation appears in source.

tags.description:
Further provenance tokens carried verbatim — an agent id, a session tag,
a scene cue. Retained so nothing on the line is dropped (koan 4).

Assignment.description: A `hyp := true|false` valuation: rule a bundle hypothesis true or false.

hyp.description: The hypothesis name being valued (the first non-operator word).

value.description: The value assigned (the last `true`/`false` word on the line).

AtomExpr.description: A predicate applied to a list of argument terms, e.g. `adjacent(a, b)`.

subject.description: The entity the slot is about.

BodyLiteral.description:
One literal of a rule body: an atom on a polarity rail.

A positive literal ([`negated`](BodyLiteral::negated) is `false`) joins over
the relation and binds its variables; a negated literal filters against the
certain layer and binds nothing (datalog safety: every variable in a negated
literal must also appear in a positive body atom).

negated.description: Whether the atom is negated (`not <atom>` at the surface).

CitationRef.description: A reference to a decision-ledger entry, e.g. `D-0042`.

Clause.description: One normalized interior line of a keyword-fronted block.

span.description: Where the clause appears in source.

CompositionStep.description: One composition step: a slot role filled by a named morpheme.

CondExpr.description: A boolean condition over named hypotheses that gates a claim.

modulus.description: The cycle modulus, if written (`cycle tide(4)`).

spokes.description: The ordered spoke names around the cycle.

Datalog.description:
A datalog derivation rule: one head atom and its body conjunction of
literals. Produced by the front end from a `head :- body` clause; consumed by
the evaluator's typed rule intake.

body.description: The body conjunction of literals (a negated literal is `not <atom>`).

head.description: The head atom derived when the body holds.

Decl.description:
A top-level declaration.

The gentle subset — [`Entity`](Decl::Entity), [`Attr`](Decl::Attr),
[`Fact`](Decl::Fact), [`Question`](Decl::Question), [`Before`](Decl::Before),
[`Hypothesis`](Decl::Hypothesis) — is fully typed. The expert tier keeps a
typed header and a captured [`Clause`] body.

oneOf.description: `<subject>.<attr> = <value>` — a slot fact about an entity.
`rule <name> [over <domain>] …` — a checker rule (world, order, or season).
`variant <path>` — a lore variant of an artifact.

DialectBody.description:
The structured body of a [`DialectDecl`](crate::decl::DialectDecl): its
interior clauses in source order, each pre-classified into a [`DialectItem`].

clauses.description: The structured interior clauses, in source order.

DialectClause.description:
One structured clause of a dialect body: its normalized text (retained for
exact round-trip) plus the typed payload the compiler reads.

clause.description:
The whitespace-normalized clause text and its span. Retained so the
formatter round-trips exactly.

item.description: The typed interpretation of the clause.

body.description:
The typed interior: each interior clause pre-classified into a
[`DialectItem`](crate::language::DialectItem) at parse time (LS-9), so the
language compiler reads typed AST instead of re-lexing clause text.

DialectItem.description:
The recognized interior forms of a dialect body (the grammar owned by the
language compiler, `crates/dli-world/src/language/dialect.rs`).

Each variant carries exactly the values the pre-LS-9 compiler derived from
the clause tokens, so the typed reader reproduces the old string-body result
byte-for-byte. A clause whose head keyword is not recognized is
[`Other`](DialectItem::Other) — the compiler ignored it before, and ignores
it now.

attested.description: Whether the `attested` grade word led the clause tail.

text.description: The quoted real-world basis, if written.

oneOf.description: `foreign <c> <c> …` — clusters marking a form as not-ours (lowercased).

`cluster-max <n>` — the consonant-cluster ceiling, `None` if no token
parsed as a count.

`sayability-max <n>` — the per-word syllable ceiling, `None` if no token
parsed as a count.

`stress <keyword>` — the stress rule keyword (the first tail token), if
present.

`name-kind <kind> = <role>… [ | <role>… ]` — a slot grammar, `None` if
the clause held no well-formed pattern.

`name-part <surface> …` — a morpheme declaration, typed exactly as the
top-level parser types a `name-part` line.
A clause whose head keyword the dialect grammar does not recognize.

kind.description: Which kind of entity this is.

slots.description: Indented slot facts written beneath the entity.

triple.description: Whether the surface used the leading `fact` keyword (triple form).

FileId.description: Identifier for a source file within a compilation.

body.description: Any other captured body clauses (`suppose …`, `add fact …`).

Ident.description: A named identifier with its source span.

span.description: Where the identifier appears in source.

NameBody.description:
The structured body of a [`NameDecl`](crate::decl::NameDecl): its interior
clauses in source order, each pre-classified into a [`NameItem`].

clauses.description: The structured interior clauses, in source order.

NameClause.description:
One structured clause of a name body: its normalized text (retained for exact
round-trip) plus the typed payload the compiler reads.

clause.description:
The whitespace-normalized clause text and its span. Retained so the
formatter round-trips exactly.

item.description: The typed interpretation of the clause.

body.description:
The typed interior: each interior clause (composition, bearer, provenance)
pre-classified into a [`NameItem`](crate::language::NameItem) at parse
time (LS-9), so the name compiler reads typed AST instead of re-lexing
clause text.

NameItem.description:
The recognized interior forms of a name body (the grammar owned by the
language compiler, `crates/dli-world/src/language/name.rs`).

Classification is by the clause's first token, exactly as the pre-LS-9
compiler classified it; the compiler applies the same header-first precedence
(a header composition or bearer wins; the first body provenance wins) when it
reads these.

oneOf.description:
`= <role> <morpheme> [ + <role> <morpheme> … ]` — the composition steps
(empty when the clause held no well-formed `role morpheme` step).

`bearer <entity> [<provenance>]` — the entity that bears the name and any
provenance riding the same line.

entity.description: The bearer entity, if a token followed `bearer`.

provenance.description: Provenance parsed from the line's tail, if any.

oneOf.description: A clause the name grammar does not recognize.

NameKindSpec.description:
A `name-kind` slot grammar: the name kind and its admissible slot-role
sequences (alternatives split by `|`).

kind.description: The name kind this grammar governs (e.g. `person.given`, `place`).

implies.description: The atom this option implies, if written.

head.description: Remaining header tokens (`family plot mission pass`).
Remaining header tokens (`speaker protagonist in spoken-proof`).

ProvenanceMarker.description:
The leading provenance word a claim carries.

A claim's *standing* is not stored (DL-0003: there is no status slot); it is
derived from this marker together with the citations behind it. The marker
records only where the claim came from — an agent's proposal or a ledger
ruling — and which register of ruling it was.

oneOf.description: `proposed` — an agent's claim, awaiting a ruling. Carries no citation.
`provisional <d-id>` — a provisional ruling, open to revision.

RatifyBody.description:
The structured body of a [`RatifyDecl`](crate::decl::RatifyDecl): the
hypothesis valuation lines it carries, plus the decision ids its lines cite.

citations.description:
The decision ids cited across the body lines, harvested at parse time so
the citation gate reads them without re-scanning clause text.

clauses.description: The valuation clauses, in source order.

RatifyClause.description:
One clause of a ratify body: its normalized text (retained for exact
round-trip) plus the typed hypothesis assignment it makes, if any.

assignment.description: The `hyp := true|false` assignment this clause makes, if it is one.

clause.description:
The whitespace-normalized clause text and its span. Retained so the
formatter round-trips exactly.

body.description:
The typed interior: the `h-cymric := true` valuation lines and the
decision ids the body cites, structured at parse time (LS-9), so the
language compiler and the citation gate read typed AST instead of
re-lexing clause text.

clauses.description: The structured block-body clauses (indented or braced), in source order.

inline.description:
The inline `head : body` clause carried on the rule line itself, present
only when the header holds a `:`/`:-` separator and the block body is
empty. It is rendered from the header tokens, never as a body line, so
the surface round-trips; the loader reads its structure here.

RuleClause.description: One structured clause of a rule body.

clause.description:
The whitespace-normalized clause text and its span. Retained so the
formatter round-trips exactly and the order/season domain engines read
their own micro-grammar off it without re-entering the front end.

datalog.description:
The world-rule datalog structure, present when this clause is a clean
`head :- body` (or `head : body`) derivation rule. `None` for an
order/season domain clause or a clause that is not clean datalog — the
world loader turns a `None` in a world rule into a malformed-rule
finding, exactly as it did when it re-parsed the text itself.

body.description:
The typed body: world-rule datalog pre-parsed into
[`Datalog`](crate::rule::Datalog); order/season clauses retained as text
for their domain engines (LS-9, `docs/design-notes/lorestore-roadmap.md`).

domain.description:
The domain the rule is enforced over: `None` is a world rule, `over order`
an episode-ordering constraint, `over season` a season-ledger rule.

head.description:
Header tokens after the name (and any `over <domain>`), before the body
(e.g. `severity error`, or the inline `head : body` datalog tokens).

RuleDomain.description:
The domain a `rule` is enforced over, routing it to the right checker engine.

A rule with no domain is a world (derivation) rule; `over order` routes to the
episode-ordering engine, `over season` to the season-ledger engine. The three
forms unify the surface under one `rule` keyword (the domain is stated, not
keyword-encoded).

ScopeHeader.description: A `scope <name>` header naming what the document's claims are about.

Span.description: A half-open byte range within a single source file.

file.description: The file this span points into.

name.description: The state name (may be dotted, e.g. `gwern.water-status`).

value.description: The value the state takes, if written.

Term.description: A term: a variable, symbol, literal, or time reference.

oneOf.description: A ground symbol naming an entity.
A reference into the time domain.

TimeClause.description: A temporal clause attached to an entity or fluent.

oneOf.description: `since <event>` — holds from the named event forward.
`until <event>` — holds up to the named event.
`< a < b < c` — an era precedence chain rooted at this entity.

TimeRef.description: A reference to a named era or event on the timeline.
